subject: Culture
title: Eternal Flames
description: A quick, practical guide to Eternal Flames.

hook.text: John F. Kennedy's grave has an eternal flame. Jackie Kennedy requested it, modeled on the flame at the Arc de Triomphe.

buildup.text: Eternal flames appear at war memorials, temples, and national monuments worldwide as symbols of undying memory.

discovery.text: Zoroastrian fire temples keep flames burning for centuries. One in Iran has burned continuously for over 1,500 years.

twist.text: The Olympic flame traces to ancient Greek myth where fire was stolen from the gods. Every torch relay repeats the story.

climax.text: Fire transcends culture as a death symbol because it transforms without destroying—it changes form, not substance.

punchline.text: A flame is a promise that remembering never stops.

quiz.question: Whose grave features an eternal flame inspired by the Arc de Triomphe?

details.summary: Eternal flames burn at memorials, tombs, and sacred sites worldwide — from JFK's grave to India's Amar Jawan Jyoti. These perpetual fires symbolize undying memory, sacrifice, and the human determination to resist death's finality through an unextinguishable symbol of life.
details.whyItMatters: Eternal flames represent humanity's most primal response to death — keeping a light burning against the darkness. They demonstrate how physical fire becomes a metaphor for immortal memory.
takeaways: Eternal flames memorialize military sacrifice at national monuments
JFK's eternal flame at Arlington was lit by Jackie Kennedy in 1963
Zoroastrian sacred fires have burned continuously for centuries

faq.question: How do eternal flames stay lit?
faq.answer: Modern eternal flames use natural gas piped to the memorial site, with electric igniters that relight the flame if wind extinguishes it. JFK's flame at Arlington uses a constant gas supply with an automatic relight system.

faq.question: What is the oldest eternal flame?
faq.answer: The Zoroastrian Atash Behram in Yazd, Iran, is said to have burned since 470 CE — over 1,500 years. Natural eternal flames also exist, like the Baba Gurgur fire in Iraq (burning for thousands of years from natural gas seepage).
